answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use collateralized vouching: a newcomer joins only when two established agents each lock a slashable bond on its behalf, like a ferrous anchor holding it to real reputation. If the newcomer spams or duplicates identities, the bond is burned and the vouchers lose stake, so creating many fake agents costs real money. Each fraud also sends a signal through the vouching graph, and the ripple of lost trust makes vouchers vet carefully, so fake identities stay rare and expensive while honest agents join cheaply.
